newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's North-West Shipping plans restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Russia's North-West Shipping plans restructuring.

text.p: The board of directors of Russia's North-West Shipping has decided to create a wholly-owned subsidiary shipping unit, the head of the company's information analysis department said.
"AO SZP (Severo-Zapadnoe Parokhodstvo) has a very cumbersome structure. We are trying to cut off the most liquid assets into the subsidiary, so that we can save them," said Alexander Mazo.
Shareholders would vote on the proposal at the annual meeting in the first half of April, he said, adding that the board made the decision in light of losses at the company.
It lost 70.5 billion roubles in the first half of 1996 according to Russian accounting standards. In 1995 pretax profits were 958 million roubles but there was no net profit.
Coopers and Lybrand will conduct an audit of 1996 results according to international accounting principles, Mazo said.
He said most of the company's fleet, with an average age of 16-17 years, would be given to the subsidiary.

He said that the Cherepovetskoi river port would also be made into a separate, wholly-owned subsidiary, though he said that an option for 19 percent of that subsidiary would be offered to the company workers after a year.

Major shareholders of the company include AKB MFK with 25 percent, Cutno Ltd with 10.8 percent, KM Invest with 8.7 percent, ULM Enterprises with 8.1 percent and ZAO Lenstroiinvestmenedzhment with 3.8 percent.
Workers own 12-15 percent of the company and CS First Boston is the nominal holder of 9.65 percent.
